attributes.body_ja:
「物（もの）と思（おも）う」は、「(A) だと信（しん）じている」や「(A) の確信（かくしん）がある」といった意味（いみ）で使（つか）われる文型（ぶんけい）です。これは、名詞（めいし）「物（もの）」、格助詞（かくじょし）「と」、そして五段動詞（ごだんどうし）「思（おも）う」からできています。ここでの「物（もの）」は、話（はな）し手（て）がそれを確（たし）かだと信（しん）じている事柄（ことがら）を指（さ）しています。

「物（もの）」は名詞（めいし）なので、この文型（ぶんけい）は連体形（れんたいけい）の語（ご）の後（うし）ろに置（お）かれます。

「思（おも）う」が過去形（かこけい）になる場合（ばあい）は、「(A) が本当（ほんとう）だと信（しん）じていた」や「(A) だと思（おも）い込（こ）んでいた」といった過去（かこ）の意味（いみ）になります。

これは硬（かた）めの表現（ひょうげん）ではありますが、日常会話（にちじょうかいわ）でもたまに使（つか）われることがあります。
attributes.body:
物（もの）と思（おも）う is made up of the noun 物（もの） 'thing', the case marking particle と, and the う-Verb 思（おも）う 'to think'. Regular translations include 'to believe that (A)', or 'to have confidence that (A)'. In a broader sense, this grammar pattern is just making use of one of the meanings of 物（もの） as being something abstract that the speaker can reliably determine has all of the qualities of something concrete.

As もの is a noun, this pattern may follow any word in its attributive form.

When 思（おも）う appears in the past tense, the most common translation is 'as I had believed was true of (A)', or 'I was under the impression that (A)'.

Although this grammar construction is slightly formal, it may occasionally be heard in daily speech.

Both expressions state an assumption, but they differ in time perspective and speaker stance. ものと思っていた looks back on a past assumption and is often used when the speaker realizes that the belief was mistaken or no longer holds true, frequently carrying a nuance of surprise or correction upon learning the reality. By contrast, ものと思う expresses a present assumption or belief that the speaker currently holds, often with confidence, and is used to state what the speaker thinks is true or likely at the time of speaking.
